Schedule 2-hour lab session next week to run NimbleHealth sample workload on Dedicated pool

header:
Date: 2026-01-17 | Start: 09:32 PST | Duration: 53m
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Anya Patel (Redwood Solutions), Priya Rao (NimbleHealth ML Lead), Tom Ellis (NimbleHealth SRE), Marcus Li (CTO), Janelle (Data Ops)
summary: Redwood walked through Optimize quantization profiles focusing on INT8 and FP8 tradeoffs. Covered console walkthrough, end-to-end benchmark interpretation, and a proposed canary rollout plan for NimbleHealth's latency-sensitive summarization service. Customer agreed to run pilot on Dedicated pool and to share prompt set and baseline metrics.
topics: INT8 vs FP8 quality delta on summarization tasks
latency P95/P99 tradeoffs and batching impact
transcript:
[00:00] Laura (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on — we want to be mindful of time, we've got 53 minutes, is this still good?
[00:07] Priya (NimbleHealth): Yes, yep, we have time. We're most interested in the fidelity tradeoffs. Our product is user-facing summaries so hallucination margin is low.
[00:15] Diego (SE): Great, quick agenda: console demo of Optimize, show INT8/FP8 profiles, then walk through what the latency numbers mean for your 99th percentile targets, then rollout plan. Sound good?
[00:27] Tom (SRE): Yep, also want to validate we can hit P99 < 350ms for 512-token inputs at our 50 RPS baseline.
[00:34] Laura: Cool — Priya, can you remind us of your current stack and where inference runs today?
[00:40] Priya: Sure — currently on prem-ish, sorry it's hybrid, we use dedicated GPU nodes in our private cloud with a homegrown REST endpoint. Model is an open decoder-arch we call "nova-small" (not exact naming), 8B-ish. We batch at 4 tokens and do a simple prefix cache.
[00:55] Diego: When you say prefix cache, is that at application layer or at the model runtime?
[01:00] Priya: App layer today, which means cold starts are heavier.
[01:05] Diego: Okay that aligns — Redwood's runtime offers KV/prefix caching at the serving layer which tends to reduce per-token latency for repeated prompts. We'll show that.
[01:15] Marcus (CTO): Quick compliance note — we need audit logs and an SSO integration; Anya, can you mark that?
[01:21] Anya: noted, we have SOC2 docs and SAML SSO flow; I'll link both.
[01:25] [00:01:25] Laura: Jumping into the console, so here on Optimize we have pre-built "precision profiles". The default is FP16/FP32 path, then we have INT8 and experimental FP8.
[01:40] Diego: Important nuance — INT8 gives biggest cost wins but can widen quality variance for some prompts; FP8 often sits between FP16 and INT8 on quality but can get low-level speedups on newer kernels.
[01:53] Priya: Can you show a concrete example for summarization?
[01:56] Diego: Yeah, let's pull up the evaluation panel: here's our blind eval run we did last week on a 200-sample summarization set. The sheet linked has ROUGE and human error flags. In INT8 we saw a median ROUGE drop of ~1.2 points, worst-case prompts dropped ~4-5 points; FP8 medians dropped ~0.5.
[02:15] Tom: Those worst-case prompts — are they long context or rare tokenization patterns?
[02:20] Diego: Mostly long context and some rare entity names where quantization interacts with softmax head slightly differently. There's also an interaction with prompt-engineering — like when you use very specific system instructions.
[02:30] Priya: Hmm, our acceptance criteria: user visible regressions must be undetectable in random A/B at 95% for our top 3 flows.
[02:38] Laura: That's a good concrete threshold — you're basically asking for small-signal detection. Our suggested path is a canary: use FP8 in canary with full telemetry, if all eval metrics and RLHF-derived signals hold, roll INT8 on lower-risk routes like background summarization.
[02:55] [00:02:55] Diego: Now latency: this is a graph of P50/P95/P99 across batch sizes and token lengths. For 512 tokens at batch=1, FP8 improves P50 by ~18% and P99 by ~8% versus FP16. INT8 gives ~35% P50 and ~15% P99. But INT8 tail variance can be higher under certain memory-pressure scenarios.
[03:20] Marcus: Are those numbers on same hardware we plan to use?
[03:23] Diego: These were on NVIDIA H100 equivalent. For your Dedicated pool with A100s, we'll calibrate — A100 often has different kernel characteristics, so we recommend a short calibration run.
[03:35] Tom: Could we get the raw latency histogram? We need to plot percentiles against our SLI windows.
[03:39] Laura: Absolutely — action item to send histograms and raw traces.
[03:43] Priya: How about hallucination rates? You said worst-case prompts saw bigger drops — can we restrict INT8 to non-critical paths?
[03:50] Diego: Exactly — route policy can direct request classes by intent. For example, high-sensitivity summaries go to FP16 or FP8, lower-sensitivity background tasks can hit INT8. The Console allows per-endpoint profiles and rollouts.
[04:05] [00:04:05] Laura: Demoing the Optimize rollout page: you can create a rollout, select model variant (FP16/FP8/INT8), set traffic splits, and add guardrails — for example, if human-quality regression > 1.5 ROUGE or P99 latency > 400ms we auto rollback.
[04:25] Janelle (Data Ops): How do you detect regression? Do you need human labels?
[04:28] Diego: We support synthetic regression detectors — LM-based quality estimators, embedding-similarity checks, and you can plug in your human-in-the-loop evals. We recommend starting with automatic detectors then gating with sampled human checks.
[04:40] Marcus: What about KV cache invalidation? For our summaries we sometimes append user-specific dynamic prefixes — will caching still help?
[04:47] Diego: Caching still helps at a sub-token level; Redwood's runtime supports partial KV reuse and prefix-aware eviction. If your prefixes are highly unique, the gains shrink.
[04:57] Priya: Ok let's talk numbers for our 50 RPS baseline: will FP8 get us under 350ms P99?
[05:03] Diego: Quick back-of-envelope: if you move batch=1 and use FP8 on H100-style hardware you likely get P99 around 320-360ms depending on I/O and network. INT8 might push you to ~270-300ms but with the quality caveats mentioned.
[05:20] Tom: Network overhead — we're on private cloud, can Redwood stitch VPC peering?
[05:24] Laura: Yes, for Private deployments we do VPC connectors and can co-locate model nodes to reduce network egress. We'll share network topology docs.
[05:32] [00:05:32] Diego: I'd like to show the benchmark spreadsheet: columns are prompt_id, token_count, model_variant, ROUGE, embedding_sim, latency_p50/p95/p99, memory_use. You can filter by prompt class.
[05:45] Priya: Can you paste that sheet into the CRM?
[05:48] Laura: Will do — you'll get a link in the follow-up.
[05:52] Diego: Also note quantization knobs: per-channel scaling, outlier clipping thresholds, and a mixed-precision mode where the attention blocks stay in FP16 and only MLPs go to INT8 — that often buys you safety.
[06:08] Marcus: Mixed precision sounds appealing as a first step.
[06:11] Priya: Can we do A/B by user cohort? We want to test high-value users separately.
[06:15] Laura: Yes, rollouts can be by header, cookie, or an attribute from your auth token.
[06:19] [00:06:19] Tom: Monitoring — what do dashboards show? Token-level cost, latency, error rates?
[06:24] Diego: All of the above. We also surface model delta metrics: per-prompt quality change, and a prompt-level alerting system for sudden drift.
[06:34] Janelle: Is there instrumentation we need to add?
[06:36] Diego: Minimal: pass a stable prompt_id and session_id, include user-tier header if you want cohort splits.
[06:42] Priya: Walk me through a canary plan you'd recommend for us.
[06:46] Laura: Step 1: Baseline — collect N=500 representative calls and record latencies and quality. Step 2: Canary FP8 on 5% of traffic for top-3 flows with synthetic detectors and sampled human checks for 48 hours. Step 3: If clean, expand FP8 to 25% and run 7-day eval. Step 4: If still good, identify background flows and pilot INT8 there, while keeping FP16/FP8 for critical flows.
[07:18] [00:07:18] Priya: Who owns rollback triggers?
[07:21] Diego: You define the thresholds but Redwood can manage automated rollback if configured. We send alerts to your SRE and product channels.
[07:30] Marcus: Cost question — what is the typical cost delta between FP16/FP8/INT8?
[07:34] Diego: Roughly speaking, INT8 can be 30-60% lower per-token compute cost depending on kernel efficiency and batching; FP8 is usually 10-25% lower. Actual cost depends on your capacity and reserved pricing.
[07:47] Tom: About the kernel differences — will you optimize for our hardware if we go Dedicated?
[07:50] Diego: Yes, part of Dedicated onboarding includes a small calibration suite which picks kernels and quant settings per model and per hardware.
[07:58] [00:07:58] Priya: We also care about drift — if model output quality slowly degrades, can Optimize detect that?
[08:02] Diego: Yes, you can attach continuous evals: a set of prompts and a comparator metric. We keep history, compute deltas, and trigger alerts on sustained drops.
[08:12] Laura: Quick note on security — for Private deployment we support customer-managed KMS and audit logs are retained per your policy.
[08:19] Marcus: Good.
[08:21] [00:08:21] Diego: Now, a short demo of a sensitivity sweep: we ran automated quant sweeps across 3 models and plotted quality vs latency. Here's a scatter where x-axis is delta ROUGE and y-axis is P99 improvement. You can pick a tolerable ROUGE budget and see recommended profiles.
[08:40] Priya: That's neat. Can we automate profile selection per endpoint?
[08:44] Diego: Yes — Optimize can suggest a profile and you can accept or override. We keep the suggestion history so you can audit why a profile was chosen.
[08:53] Tom: What about training-time-aware quantization? We don't retrain.
[08:57] Diego: We focus on post-training quantization. If you wanted pruning-aware or QAT, that's a different workflow; Redwood's current tooling is PTQ with per-layer calibration.
[09:07] Priya: Ok — what's the expected lift if we follow mixed-precision first then INT8 for background?
[09:11] Diego: Typical pattern: mixed-precision gets you most of the tail safety with ~15-25% cost cut; INT8 on background gets additional 20-40% savings. So combined you could see 30-50% overall compute reductions depending on traffic mix.
[09:28] [00:09:28] Laura: Let's capture risks: possible prompt-specific regressions, potential for higher tail variance under mem pressure, and calibration time for A100/H100 differences.
[09:40] Priya: Are there examples of customer rollouts?
[09:43] Laura: Yes, we've done this with a fintech and a marketplace: fintech kept FP16 for critical flows and used INT8 for batch billing jobs, marketplace used FP8 for chat and INT8 for background ranking. We'll share anonymized case studies.
[09:58] Marcus: Timebox — do we want a live lab next week?
[10:01] Priya: Yes, recommend doing that.
[10:03] Laura: We'll schedule — Diego will bring the calibration scripts.
[10:06] [00:10:06] Diego: One more subtlety — quantization interacts with function-calling/structured outputs if your model is constrained. Tests should include your canonical prompts that exercise tool calls.
[10:17] Janelle: Good call. We'll surface a handful.
[10:20] Priya: Final question — for compliance, can logs be redacted before Redwood retains them?
[10:24] Anya: Yes, we support redaction hooks and customer-side pre-ingest filters for Private deployments.
[10:29] [00:10:29] Laura: Ok quick recap of next steps and owners — Diego will prepare the reproduce script and run a 1-hour calibration with your sample prompts; Laura will send the benchmark sheet and Optimize links; Priya and team will share prompts and baseline metrics. We'll schedule a 2-hour lab next Tue or Wed.
[10:44] Priya: Thanks, that was helpful.
[10:46] Marcus: Appreciate it.
[10:48] Laura: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials.
[10:52] [END TRANSCRIPT]
